title: Democrats Take Control of Congress in the Midterm Elections
summary:
Voters across the United States have given Democrats control of both houses of Congress. Results from the midterm elections, which closed on Tuesday, showed Democrats winning the House of Representatives as well as the Senate.

Midterm elections happen halfway through a president's four-year term, when all House seats and about a third of Senate seats are decided. This time, the results were widely seen as a setback for President Donald Trump and his Republican Party, which had previously held both chambers.

According to the Associated Press, voters were motivated by concerns including high prices, the war involving Iran, and questions about government corruption. Democrats won races in states from Texas to Iowa to New Hampshire, including some states Trump had won by large margins two years earlier.

Democratic leaders welcomed the outcome. Senate leader Chuck Schumer called it a "generational remake of the Senate map," while House leader Hakeem Jeffries said "the American people are crying out for transformational change."

President Trump said he would accept the results. He also said he would veto legislation passed by the Democratic-controlled Congress, and said voters "didn't like the candidates." Republican leaders said they would work with the president to block Democratic proposals they opposed.

Democratic leaders have said they plan to investigate members of the Trump administration and examine how the president's family has benefited from his time in office. They have also said removing Trump or his Cabinet officials from office through impeachment is not ruled out.

The new balance of power means the president's final two years in office are likely to involve much more debate, and much closer checks, from Congress.
why_it_matters: Control of Congress decides which laws can pass and how closely the president is checked, so this result will shape rules and prices that affect families across the country.

background_read: Midterm elections are held halfway through a president's four-year term, when voters choose the whole House of Representatives and about a third of the Senate.
Congress makes the country's laws, and the president can block laws by vetoing them, so control of Congress decides how easily a president can pass plans.
When Congress and the president are on opposite sides, Congress can also investigate the president's team much more closely.
That is why a midterm result can change the balance of power for the rest of a president's time in office.
